To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD5+ cells constitute a small fraction of the B-cell compartment, that the CD5+ B cell compartment is heterogeneous and that the CD5/ CD19 assay is a clinically useful assay for MRD detection.
the percentage of CD5 + B cells in the peripheral blood and bone marrow of normal subjects ranges from 3.6% to 23.9% and from 4.4% to 19.5%, respectively.
the CD5+ B cell percentage in normal peripheral blood is 12.2%, with a range of 3.6 to 23.9%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a flow cytometric assay that is useful in the diagnosis of CLL and in monitoring the course of the disease.
the development of an assay that is capable of detecting the presence of a small percentage of CLL cells among normal cells.
the development of a flow cytometric technique that is sensitive enough to detect the minimal residual disease in CLL patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reference value of CD5+ normal B cells in the blood is 3.6% to 23.9% and that the CD5/ CD19 assay is a clinically useful assay for MRD detection in CLL.
CD5+ lymphocytes in the normal range are approximately 1% to 2% of the B cells in peripheral blood and approximately 1% of the B cell in bone marrow.
the CD5/ CD19 assay is a very sensitive tool for the diagnosis of minimal residual disease in CLL and can be used for the monitoring of patients with this disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD5+ cells constitute 12% of B cells in normal blood and bone marrow and that this assay is sensitive enough to detect 1 CLL cells in 1, 000 leukocytes.
the CD5+ B cell population in normal PB is not as high as previously reported and that a CD5+ B-CLL-like-phenotype can be observed in normal PB.
the CD5/ CD19 immunofluorescence assay has a clinically significant sensitivity for MRD assessment in CLL and that a distinct "bright" subpopulation of CD5+ cells can be observed in normal samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD5+ cells are not as common as previously thought and that this assay can be used for the detection of MRD.
the CD5+/CD19+ B-cell ratio in PB and BM in normal subjects ranges from 3.6% to 23.9% and 4.4% to 19.5%, respectively.
the CD5+ B cell population in the normal bone marrow is a very useful frame of reference for MRD analysis.
